newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's CANTV plans to pay dividend in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV plans to pay dividend in 1998.

text.p: Venezuela's telephone company CANTV plans to pays its first dividend to shareholders in 1998, after its upcoming privatization, one of its top executives said.
"We expect to pay a dividend in cash in 1998 based on 1997 results," Finance Vice-President Andres Glusky told reporters.
The Venezuelan government plans to sell its 49 percent stake in CANTV this month.
The share offering will see 40 percent of the company's stock placed on local and international markets.
The share price will be known on November 21. Its reference range is currently between $3.07 and $3.50. Trading in the stock will start immediately after the offering.
Glusky spoke at the start of the Venezuelan roadshow, which is to be followed by similar ones in Europe and the United States.
He gave partial figures for CANTV results this year. In the first nine months, revenue totalled $843 million, a drop in real terms of $10 million from the same period last year.
Total revenue in 1995 reached $1.20 billion in real terms, up from $1.07 billion in 1994, Glusky told a news conference.
He also said CANTV hoped to reach an agreement with creditor banks to restructure its large foreign debt but gave no details.
However, he said outstanding debt was already reduced from $1.10 billion at end-1994 to $700 million today. Average repayment period was now four years up from 120 days in 1994.
CANTV was partially privatized in 1991 when a consortium led by GTE Corp bought 40 percent of the stock at about $4.70 a share.
